notes:
Summary: PrimeVector UCore is an adtech platform that performs real-time bidding (RTB) scoring and personalization at the edge of their exchange. Very latency- and cost-sensitive: they pay per-impression and need predictable p99 latency under heavy spikes. They are skeptical of quantization because rerank quality directly impacts revenue, but very open to Redwood's Optimize suggestions if we can show negligible quality delta.

Key requirements:
- Workload: hybrid of tiny prompt reranks (~30-80 tokens) and embedding lookups for user profiles.
- Latency target: p99 <= 35ms for rerank path (ideal 25-30ms).
- Throughput: baseline 2k req/s with headroom for 6k req/s bursts (peak region).
- Cost sensitivity: target effective token cost that keeps compute < $X per million impressions (quote: 'If we can't hit cost floor, we'll self-host').
- Model preferences: open-vendor medium-size transformer (7B-13B family) for rerank; embeddings models small/quantized.
- Routing/fallback: want ability to route to a cheaper quantized variant on overload and fall back to higher-quality float variant when latency headroom allows.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown per route, tracing for per-request latency, retention 90 days for audit.

Direct quotes from CTO on call: "If we can get p99 under 35ms and cost down 30% vs our current infra, we move to Dedicated. But quality cannot drop more than 1-2% revenue impact."

POC ask: Redwood to deliver a benchmark report with (1) steady-state and spike perf numbers (p50/p95/p99), (2) batching and prefix caching configs tested, (3) quantized vs fp16 quality/latency/cost comparison on rerank set, (4) recommended Dedicated pool sizes and autoscale policy for predictable headroom.
